newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends down, awaits U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends down, awaits U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Shares ended fair trade lower on Thursday after a strong start, as investors took profits from recent strength and buyers withdrew ahead of U.S. August jobless data due on Friday, brokers said.
The HEX index fell 0.64 percent to 2,090.87, with volume a steady 341 million markka, 47 percent of it in Nokia.
Stocks are traditionally weak in September and October, one broker said; he expected little vigour on Friday with no home-grown company news due.

Forestry group UPM-Kymmene fell 1.30 markka to 99.60 -- below 100 resistance crossed last month -- after it said it had launched a U.S. ADR programme for OTC markets. Some investors had hoped for a proper New York listing for the stock.
"It was not received positively, but then again not very negatively either ... a full NYSE listing was perhaps what had been more expected," one broker said.

Nokia closed lively trade 0.10 markka up at 185.90 after earlier being depressed by fears that Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), the fund management arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, may have to sell some of its 1.5 billion markka stake.
Daily Kauppalehti reported on Wednesday that Nokia could be among the reasons for huge losses at MGAM, which has 10 percent of its investments in Nokia.
Raision Tehtaat closed fair trade down 19.00 markka at 299.00, under pressure from profit-taking and as it announced a 60 million markka malt production expansion.
Paper machine maker Valmet was also hit by profit-taking, falling 1.30 markka to 74.50 despite it announcing a 200 million markka paper machine rebuild order from Stora.
